title: Matthew Chapter 10 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Matthew chapter 10 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Matthew Chapter 10 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Matthew Chapter 10.

questions.question: In Matthew 10, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: Jesus giving the twelve disciples power against unclean spirits
Jesus sending the twelve apostles to the lost sheep of Israel
Jesus commanding the twelve not to enter cities of Samaritans
Jesus listing the names of the twelve apostles
questions.correctAnswer: Jesus giving the twelve disciples power against unclean spirits
questions.explanation: Matthew 10:1 shows Jesus giving power to the twelve disciples before he lists their names or sends them out.

questions.question: Who is listed first among the twelve apostles in Matthew 10?
questions.explanation: Matthew 10:2 states the first named apostle is Simon, who is called Peter.

questions.question: Which brothers are named together among the twelve apostles?
questions.explanation: Matthew 10:2 mentions James the son of Zebedee and John his brother.

questions.question: What was Matthew's occupation before becoming an apostle?
questions.explanation: Matthew 10:3 calls Matthew the publican, meaning tax collector.

questions.question: Which apostle is described as the one who betrayed Jesus?
questions.explanation: Matthew 10:4 identifies Judas Iscariot as the one who also betrayed Jesus.

questions.question: Where were the twelve apostles commanded NOT to go?
options: Into the way of the Gentiles
To the lost sheep of Israel
questions.correctAnswer: Into the way of the Gentiles
questions.explanation: Matthew 10:5 states Jesus commanded them not to go into the way of the Gentiles or any city of the Samaritans.

questions.question: To whom were the twelve apostles told to go instead?
options: The lost sheep of the house of Israel
questions.correctAnswer: The lost sheep of the house of Israel
questions.explanation: Matthew 10:6 instructs them to go to the lost sheep of the house of Israel.

questions.question: What message were the twelve apostles to preach as they went?
options: The kingdom of heaven is at hand
questions.correctAnswer: The kingdom of heaven is at hand
questions.explanation: Matthew 10:7 says they were to preach, saying, 'The kingdom of heaven is at hand.'

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT one of the miracles the apostles were told to perform?
questions.explanation: Matthew 10:8 lists miracles including healing the sick, cleansing lepers, raising the dead, and casting out devils; parting the sea is not mentioned.

questions.question: What were the apostles told about receiving and giving?
options: Freely ye have received, freely give
questions.correctAnswer: Freely ye have received, freely give
questions.explanation: Matthew 10:8 instructs them to freely give because they have freely received.

questions.question: What were the apostles instructed NOT to provide for themselves on their journey?
options: Gold, silver, or brass in their purses
questions.correctAnswer: Gold, silver, or brass in their purses
questions.explanation: Matthew 10:9 commands them not to provide gold, silver, or brass in their purses.

questions.question: True or False: Jesus told the apostles to carry two coats and shoes for their journey.
questions.explanation: Matthew 10:10 says not to take two coats, shoes, or staffs for the journey.

questions.question: True or False: The apostles were to stay in a worthy person’s house until they left that city.
questions.explanation: Matthew 10:11 instructs them to abide in the house of the worthy person until they depart.

questions.question: True or False: When entering a house, the apostles were told to salute it.
questions.explanation: Matthew 10:12 says when they come into a house, they are to salute it.

questions.question: True or False: The apostles were told to leave their peace with a house even if it was not worthy.
questions.explanation: Matthew 10:13 states if the house is not worthy, let your peace return to you.

medium.title: Matthew Chapter 10 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Matthew Chapter 10 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What will be more tolerable in the day of judgment than for that city?
options: The land of Sodom and Gomorrha
questions.correctAnswer: The land of Sodom and Gomorrha
questions.explanation: This answer is correct as stated in Matthew 10:15, where Jesus compares the judgment of cities, indicating Sodom and Gomorrha will have a lesser judgment than the unrepentant cities.

questions.question: What does Matthew 10:18 promise will happen if someone is brought before governors and kings for Jesus' sake?
options: They will have a testimony against them and the Gentiles
questions.correctAnswer: They will have a testimony against them and the Gentiles
questions.explanation: Matthew 10:18 states that being brought before governors and kings serves as a testimony against them and the Gentiles, highlighting the importance of their witness.

questions.question: What are the disciples advised to take no thought about when they are delivered up?
questions.explanation: According to Matthew 10:19, disciples are instructed to not worry about how or what they will speak, as it will be given to them in that hour.

questions.question: What does Matthew 10:22 say about those who endure to the end?
questions.explanation: Matthew 10:22 indicates that those who endure through persecution for Jesus' name will ultimately receive salvation.

questions.question: According to Matthew 10:24, how does the status of a disciple compare to that of their master?
options: The disciple is above the master
The disciple is equal to the master
The disciple is not above his master
The disciple is below the master
questions.correctAnswer: The disciple is not above his master
questions.explanation: Matthew 10:24 states clearly that a disciple holds no higher status than their master, emphasizing the expectations of following Jesus.

questions.question: What should the disciples do if they are not received in a house or city, according to Matthew 10:14?
options: Shake off the dust of their feet
questions.correctAnswer: Shake off the dust of their feet
questions.explanation: Matthew 10:14 instructs the disciples to shake off the dust of their feet as a sign against those who do not receive their message.

questions.question: In Matthew 10:27, what are the disciples encouraged to do with what they hear in darkness?
questions.explanation: Matthew 10:27 encourages the disciples to proclaim what they hear in darkness openly, demonstrating their role in spreading the truth.

questions.question: What does Matthew 10:20 indicate about who will actually speak through the disciples?
questions.explanation: In Matthew 10:20, it is stated that the Spirit of the Father will speak through the disciples, relieving them of the burden of preparing speeches.

questions.question: According to Matthew 10:28, whom should the disciples fear?
options: God who can destroy both soul and body
questions.correctAnswer: God who can destroy both soul and body
questions.explanation: Matthew 10:28 emphasizes that the disciples should revere God, who has power over both physical life and eternal destiny.

questions.question: What does the warning in Matthew 10:17 suggest about the treatment of the disciples?
questions.explanation: Matthew 10:17 warns the disciples that they will be delivered to councils and scourged, indicating the severity of the persecution they will encounter.

questions.question: In Matthew 10:25, how does the treatment of Jesus relate to that of His disciples?
options: They will be treated the same
They will not be treated at all
questions.correctAnswer: They will be treated the same
questions.explanation: Matthew 10:25 states that if Jesus, the master, is called Beelzebub, the disciples can expect similar treatment, reinforcing the idea of shared experience in persecution.

questions.question: Matthew 10:23 advises the disciples to flee to another city when they are persecuted. What does this imply about their mission?
questions.explanation: The instruction in Matthew 10:23 to flee indicates that the mission is ongoing and that they will continue spreading the message until the Son of Man returns.

questions.question: Is it true that the disciples are told to fear men who can kill the body?
questions.explanation: This is false because Matthew 10:28 specifically instructs them not to fear those who can kill the body, but instead to fear God.

questions.question: Is it true that the disciples are warned about being delivered to councils and scourged?
questions.explanation: This is true as stated in Matthew 10:17, where Jesus warns the disciples about the persecution they will face.

questions.question: Is it true that Jesus gave His disciples authority over unclean spirits to heal all manner of sickness?
questions.explanation: This is false because while Jesus gave the disciples power to cast out unclean spirits and heal, it is not stated as 'all manner of sickness' in a way that implies they had absolute control, rather they were to exercise authority as given by Him.

hard.title: Matthew Chapter 10 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Matthew Chapter 10.

questions.question: What should one not fear according to Matthew 10:31?
questions.explanation: This is correct because Matthew 10:31 states, 'Fear ye not therefore, ye are of more value than many sparrows.'

questions.question: In Matthew 10:32, what will Jesus do for those who confess Him before men?
questions.explanation: This is correct because Matthew 10:32 says, 'Whosoever therefore shall confess me before men, him will I confess also before my Father which is in heaven.'

questions.question: According to Matthew 10:34, what does Jesus say He has come to bring?
questions.explanation: This is correct because Matthew 10:34 states, 'Think not that I am come to send peace on earth: I came not to send peace, but a sword.'

questions.question: Who does Jesus say will be a man's foes in Matthew 10:36?
questions.explanation: This is correct because Matthew 10:36 states, 'And a man's foes shall be they of his own household.'

questions.question: What does Matthew 10:39 indicate about finding one's life?
questions.explanation: This is correct because Matthew 10:39 states, 'He that findeth his life shall lose it: and he that loseth his life for my sake shall find it.'

questions.question: What does the Greek word 'akouo' mean in Matthew 10:14?
questions.explanation: 'Akouo' means 'to hear,' which is significant in Matthew 10:14 where it refers to those who will not hear the disciples' words.

questions.question: Which literary technique is used in Matthew 10:35 when Jesus mentions family divisions?
questions.explanation: Matthew 10:35 uses parallelism as it presents contrasting relationships, emphasizing divisions within families.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage connects to the theme of confessing Christ as seen in Matthew 10:32?
questions.explanation: Romans 10:9 connects with Matthew 10:32 as it states, 'That if thou shalt confess with thy mouth the Lord Jesus, and shalt believe in thine heart that God hath raised him from the dead, thou shalt be saved.'

questions.question: Which other Bible passage connects to the theme of valuing life mentioned in Matthew 10:39?
questions.explanation: John 12:25 states, 'He that loveth his life shall lose it; and he that hateth his life in this world shall keep it unto life eternal,' echoing the theme found in Matthew 10:39.

questions.question: What comes directly before the statement in Matthew 10:30 about the hairs of your head being numbered?
questions.explanation: Matthew 10:30 follows Matthew 10:31, which begins with 'Fear ye not therefore,' emphasizing the reassurance provided in the verses.

questions.question: What comes directly after Jesus' statement about taking up one's cross in Matthew 10:38?
questions.explanation: Matthew 10:39 follows Matthew 10:38, continuing the theme of sacrifice and the paradox of life.

questions.question: In Matthew 10:41, what is the reward for receiving a prophet?
questions.explanation: Matthew 10:41 states, 'He that receiveth a prophet in the name of a prophet shall receive a prophet's reward,' emphasizing the importance of recognizing God's messengers.

questions.question: In Matthew 10:42, what does Jesus say about giving a cup of cold water to little ones?
options: You shall in no wise lose your reward
questions.correctAnswer: You shall in no wise lose your reward
questions.explanation: This is correct as Matthew 10:42 states, 'verily I say unto you, he shall in no wise lose his reward,' highlighting the value of even small acts of kindness.

questions.question: True or False: According to Matthew 10:30, God knows the number of hairs on your head.
questions.explanation: This is correct as Matthew 10:30 states, 'But the very hairs of your head are all numbered,' affirming God's intimate knowledge of individuals.

questions.question: True or False: Jesus came to bring peace according to Matthew 10:34.
questions.explanation: This is correct as Matthew 10:34 states, 'I came not to send peace, but a sword,' indicating a mission that may cause division.

theological.title: Matthew Chapter 10 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Matthew Chapter 10 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Matthew 10:8 teach about the nature of salvation and ministry?
options: Salvation and ministry are to be freely given as freely received
Salvation is earned through works of healing
Only the spiritually elite can perform miracles
questions.correctAnswer: Salvation and ministry are to be freely given as freely received
questions.explanation: Matthew 10:8 states, 'freely ye have received, freely give,' teaching that the gifts of salvation and ministry are not to be commercialized but shared freely.

questions.question: What doctrine about discipleship is taught in Matthew 10:38?
options: Taking up one’s cross is essential to true discipleship
Followers of Christ are exempt from suffering
questions.correctAnswer: Taking up one’s cross is essential to true discipleship
questions.explanation: Matthew 10:38 emphasizes that the disciple must 'taketh not his cross, and followeth after me,' showing that self-denial and suffering are integral to following Christ.

questions.question: What doctrine about divine revelation and judgment is taught in Matthew 10:26?
options: Nothing hidden will remain secret; all will be revealed
God withholds judgment until the end of the world
Faith is a private matter with no public consequences
Only the righteous will know hidden truths
questions.correctAnswer: Nothing hidden will remain secret; all will be revealed
questions.explanation: Matthew 10:26 teaches that 'there is nothing covered, that shall not be revealed,' affirming God's ultimate disclosure and judgment.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Matthew 10:20 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: Matthew 10:20 says 'the Spirit of your Father which speaketh in you,' showing God's immanence—His presence and activity within believers.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Matthew 10:29–30 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: Verses 29–30 describe how not even a sparrow falls without the Father’s knowledge and that all the hairs on the head are numbered, demonstrating God's omniscience.

questions.question: How does Matthew 10:14–15 connect to broader biblical themes of judgment and responsibility?
options: It prepares for final judgment by stressing accountability for rejecting the gospel
It abolishes all judgment for unbelievers
It promises universal salvation regardless of reception
It limits judgment to only Gentile nations
questions.correctAnswer: It prepares for final judgment by stressing accountability for rejecting the gospel
questions.explanation: Matthew 10:14–15 warns that cities rejecting the apostles will face harsher judgment than Sodom, linking to themes of judgment and divine justice.

questions.question: What redemptive-historical theme is prepared for by Matthew 10:16's depiction of believers as 'sheep in the midst of wolves'?
options: The persecution of the church before Christ's return
The peaceable kingdom with no conflict
The political triumph of Israel over Gentiles
questions.correctAnswer: The persecution of the church before Christ's return
questions.explanation: Matthew 10:16 metaphorically describes believers facing hostile opposition, anticipating the church’s persecution motif in redemptive history.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Matthew 10:32 and 10:33 teach about confession and denial?
options: Confessing Christ publicly results in Christ's acknowledgment before God, while denying Him leads to denial before God
Private faith alone suffices without public confession
Denial of Christ has no eternal consequences
Confession is only necessary for clergy
questions.correctAnswer: Confessing Christ publicly results in Christ's acknowledgment before God, while denying Him leads to denial before God
questions.explanation: Verses 32 and 33 affirm the doctrine that public confession or denial has eternal consequences before the Father in heaven.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Matthew 10:22 and 10:39 teach about perseverance and salvation?
options: Endurance to the end is necessary for salvation, and true life is found through losing one's life for Christ
Faith without endurance is sufficient for salvation
Losing life for Christ leads to condemnation
questions.correctAnswer: Endurance to the end is necessary for salvation, and true life is found through losing one's life for Christ
questions.explanation: Matthew 10:22 teaches endurance leads to salvation, and 10:39 teaches losing life for Christ results in finding true life, linking perseverance and salvation.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Matthew 10:40 and 10:41 teach about receiving messengers of God?
options: Receiving God's messengers is equivalent to receiving God and results in rewards
Receiving messengers is optional without spiritual consequence
questions.correctAnswer: Receiving God's messengers is equivalent to receiving God and results in rewards
questions.explanation: Verses 40 and 41 teach that receiving apostles or prophets is tantamount to receiving Christ and God, and such hospitality brings rewards.

questions.question: Sceptics claim Matthew 10:17-20 encourages passive acceptance of persecution without preparation. What does this passage actually teach?
options: Believers will be guided by the Spirit in what to say during trials
Believers should avoid all confrontation to escape persecution
Persecution is not promised to disciples
Believers must prepare elaborate defenses without reliance on God
questions.correctAnswer: Believers will be guided by the Spirit in what to say during trials
questions.explanation: Verses 17-20 teach that though persecution comes, the Spirit will provide words, indicating divine enablement rather than passive resignation.

questions.question: What doctrine about divine provision and trust is taught in Matthew 10:9-10?
options: Ministers should rely on God’s provision rather than material resources
Ministers must accumulate resources for security
Material wealth is a sign of God’s favor
questions.correctAnswer: Ministers should rely on God’s provision rather than material resources
questions.explanation: Matthew 10:9-10 instructs ministers not to take gold or provisions, emphasizing trust in God's provision during ministry.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is highlighted in Matthew 10:28 regarding fear and judgment?
questions.explanation: Matthew 10:28 teaches to fear God who can destroy both soul and body in hell, demonstrating God's omnipotence over life and eternal judgment.

questions.question: How does Matthew 10:34-36 fulfill a theme elsewhere in Scripture related to Christ's mission?
options: It fulfills the theme of division caused by Christ’s gospel within families
It teaches universal peace and harmony without conflict
It anticipates political overthrow of Israel’s enemies
It denies any social consequences of faith
questions.correctAnswer: It fulfills the theme of division caused by Christ’s gospel within families
questions.explanation: Verses 34-36 describe division within households caused by Christ, fulfilling prophetic themes of the cost of discipleship and gospel division.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Matthew 10:23 and 10:25 teach about the nature of discipleship and eschatology?
options: Discipleship involves suffering and fleeing, and the Son of Man’s coming is near
Disciples will conquer earthly kingdoms before Christ’s return
The coming of the Son of Man is distant and unrelated to discipleship
Discipleship guarantees worldly peace and security
questions.correctAnswer: Discipleship involves suffering and fleeing, and the Son of Man’s coming is near
questions.explanation: Verse 23 advises fleeing persecution, while 23 also states the Son of Man’s coming before the apostles complete their mission, linking discipleship with eschatology.
